body: ₹294 (May 2020) → ATH ₹5,490 (Oct 2024) ≈19x (≈310x from the 2008 low ₹17.7). Trailing P/E 155 → 232 (only 1.5x), so implied EPS rose ~12.5x and the move was earnings-driven even though the starting P/E looked absurd: COVID had depressed EPS. Revenue FY21 ₹2,593 cr → FY26 ₹20,074 cr; OPM 4% → 19%; ROCE 1% → ~31%. Drawdown inside the run only −22%; −43% in COVID (Feb–May 2020). Early signal: Zudio, a low-price fashion format, was opening hundreds of stores with fast paybacks. Store adds and like-for-like (LFL) growth were disclosed in quarterly updates, and Westside margins held. An alert investor could have read the unit economics rather than the trailing P/E. Ended/stalled: LFL growth slowed from double digits to low single digits or negative in FY26, newer Tier-2 stores had lower sales throughput, and there were repeated sell-offs on business updates (Apr, Jul, Oct, Nov 2025; −10% in Jul 2026). The stock fell −59% to ₹2,266 (Mar 2026) and is ₹3,225 on 19 Nov 2026 (P/E ~90). Lesson: a high trailing P/E is not disqualifying when earnings are cyclically depressed and unit economics are visible. In retail, LFL deceleration is the exit signal.

title: Trent 2020–2024: Zudio store economics, ~19x on earnings despite 150x start
